performance.scope: Six fresh processes per runtime and all source-load permutations. Twelve balanced common >=20ms batches per workflow, same-source duplicate, pre-timing numerical/alias/caller-state checks. Twenty existing public0.71API flows and seven independently checked pure-callback JVP compositions of released0.71 public AD primitives. The new functionalJVP API has no released0.71 counterpart. No nativeTorch/GPU/cold-start/universal speedup claim.

findings: All18fresh processes and27flows passed exact-source,program,numerical,dtype/shape,alias and caller-state checks.

Existing20public API workflows have B/A medians0.9913–1.0164 and B/duplicate0.9918–1.0132; A/A0.9924–1.0079. No material persistent existing-API regression requiring additional controls was identified within this experiment. Not a universal no-regression claim.

Seven newJVP workflows cost6.4%–13.6% more than the qualified pure-callback released0.71 publicAD compositions. Those compositions are not a released0.71functionalJVP API or a generic semantic substitute. This is feature overhead,not an isolated-cause measurement or speedup claim.

NewJVP CPU tracked allocation peaks are2.4%–6.3% higher than those compositions; corresponding A/A peaks1.0000–1.0018. The three existing HVP peaks follow their A/A controls. One process,six balanced orders; not RSS,WASM/GPU memory,latency or universal gains.

The compatibility and returned-graph features justify continuing full application validation with the measured costs disclosed. Earlier prototype optimization timings remain historical,not selected-source performance evidence.

cpu_allocations.scope: One CPU process,ten API workflows,six balanced call orders. Tracemalloc peaks include retained output graphs where requested. Not RSS,WASM/GPU memory,latency,isolated-cause or universal improvement evidence.

additional_cpu_unsupported_boundary.scope: Tensor.add_ on a captured vector before/after the callback output,create_graph false/true. Native supports this; selected candidate explicitly rejects. Additional boundary evidence,not part of the2304inventory or a native-compatible feature claim.

limitations: Real float32/64 functionalJVP with ordinary reverse queries of returned graphs; no general higher-order reverse AD,complex/nested transforms,callback hook registration,in-place Tensor mutations inside forward AD or GPU backend.

88JVP cases use explicit mathematical controls for qualified fused-normalization/singular-determinant graph discrepancies;32callback hook combinations explicitly reject. Not literal native graph equivalence.
Seven newJVP performance references are independently qualified pure-callback compositions of released0.71 publicAD primitives,not an existing0.71functionalJVP API.
CPU allocation peaks are one process,ten specific API workflows,six balanced call orders. Not RSS,WASM/GPU memory,latency or universal gains.
